title: observability: automate Prometheus/Grafana + log shipping for Private installs, add TF modules & upgrade hooks
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Automates Prometheus/Grafana deployment for Private installs; adds Terraform modules for metrics and log provisioning; includes curated dashboards and alert rules; adds upgrade/rollback hooks to ensure observability components are reconciled during installer upgrades.
body:
Motivation:
Private (VPC/on-prem) customers have been asking for an automated observability bootstrap that is safe for air-gapped and managed network environments. Currently onboarding requires manual Helm installs and bespoke TF wiring. This PR bundles Helm chart updates, Terraform modules, and installer hooks to automate Prometheus + Grafana + log shipping (Vector/Fluentd) provisioning as part of the private-installer workflow.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a dedicated `observability` umbrella Helm chart under `redwood-private-installer/helm/observability` that deploys Prometheus (kube-prometheus-stack-lite), Grafana with provisioning for dashboards, and a configurable log-shipper (Vector by default, Fluentd optional).
- Introduces Terraform modules under `redwood-private-installer/terraform/modules/observability` to provision cloud-managed endpoints (when applicable), DNS records, TLS cert references, and RBAC/service accounts for metrics ingestion in VPCs.
- Installer hooks: pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hooks to gracefully drain/reconcile observability workloads during installer upgrades and perform rollbacks if alerting stack fails health checks.
- Grafana: ships curated dashboards (API latency, token usage, model-serving tails, node-level GPU metrics) and default alert rules mapped to existing paging channels. Dashboards are provisioned via ConfigMaps and a short docs section on customization.
- Adds a `observability.enable` flag to the main installer values with sensible defaults for private installs and an `observability.mode` (managed|bring-your-own) to support operator-managed stacks.

Files changed (summary):
See files_changed list for top-level touchpoints. Key files include Helm templates, TF module code, installer hook scripts, and README updates.

Testing/Validation:
- Unit: helm lint, templating checks, and terraform validate ran locally and in CI.
- Integration: full private installer end-to-end on k8s v1.25 and v1.26 in a VPC test harness; observed prometheus scrape targets, grafana dashboard provisioning, and vector shipping logs to an S3-compatible sink.
- Upgrade tests: exercised a minor and a patch upgrade where the observability hook ran and validated signals before marking upgrade complete. Rollback path validated by injecting a misconfigured alert rule, observing hook-triggered rollback.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated behind `observability.enable=false` by default.
2) Beta rollout with internal Dedicated/private pilot customers.
3) Gradual enablement and documentation updates.

Backward compatibility:
- Default is non-breaking; users who relied on manual Helm installs are unaffected.
- For BYO stacks, set `observability.mode=bring-your-own` and the installer will skip provisioning.

Checklist:
- [x] Helm chart and templates
- [x] Terraform modules and examples
- [x] Installer hooks and idempotency checks
- [x] CI integration (helm lint, tf validate, unit tests)
- [x] E2E test harness runs

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on the upgrade/rollback hooks and the idempotency of the Helm templates for cluster-restores.
- I added conservative resource requests/limits for Prometheus to make it suitable for smaller private clusters; customers can override via values.

Related: ENG-2345 (observability automation), ENG-3012 (private-installer upgrades)
